anti_overlap: Leave illocutionary act-type (assertion vs question vs directive vs expressive) to the pragmatics/speech-act lens; this lens asks only whether truth-apt content is used (asserted) or merely mentioned.
Leave sincerity and dialectical accountability to the commitment/accountability lens; a use-level assertion can still fail to be 'defensible' for reasons this lens does not adjudicate.
decision_lens: Rank the five candidates by whether each distinguishes propositional truth-aptness of embedded content from the veridicality status the author commits it to (asserted, hedged-but-asserted, quoted-not-asserted, conditionally-supposed). Penalize any candidate letting quoted or hypothetical material register as the SPEAKER's claim merely because it is truth-apt.
focus: Whether the rubric conflates a content-level property (the utterance contains truth-apt propositional material) with a use-level property (the author is presently asserting that content as true, rather than quoting, hypothesizing, or reporting it).
name: fd-semantics-propositional-veridicality
persona: Apply the perspective of a formal/truth-conditional semanticist working with computational veridicality and factuality annotation (FactBank-style asserted/negated/hedged/quoted values per proposition) and the classical use-mention distinction.
review_areas: Whether candidates place quoted/pasted third-party text (the Monopoly Go! paste, scored NO at p=0.974) outside 'claim' on use-mention grounds, vs surface cues like length that fail on shorter pastes.
Whether conditionals are handled: asserting 'if P then Q' does not assert P or Q individually — check conditional-form posts for whether a sub-clause's truth-aptness leaks into a YES verdict.
Whether hedges ('I think', '[rough/exploratory]') adjust veridicality strength (still asserted, just qualified — per the fixed p=0.852 hedge-rejection bug) rather than count as non-assertion.
Whether reported/quoted content ('as @X once said...') is distinguished from the author's own commitment, given the corpus is 74.2% replies and 22.7% quote-posts per the brainstorm.
Whether bare truth-apt backchannel tokens ('true', 'I think so') are elliptical re-assertions vs discourse markers — sample the ~387 sub-20-char posts scored claim in data/gate.jsonl.

severity_examples.condition: Corrupts the attribution invariant Decision 3 depends on (every commitment needs ≥1 norvid-authored root) — flag if a top candidate has this shape.
severity_examples.scenario: A candidate has no use/mention distinction at all, so it would systematically misattribute quoted or reported propositions to the post's author as their own commitment.

severity_examples.condition: Flag if a ranked candidate would regress this already-paid-for fix.
severity_examples.scenario: A candidate treats all hedges as disqualifying, reproducing the exact false-negative already found and fixed once: the p=0.852 rejection of the hedged phase-transitions post.

severity_examples.condition: Worth flagging as a gap regardless of overall rank.
severity_examples.scenario: A candidate is silent on bare anaphoric backchannel tokens ('true', 'I think so'), leaving ~387 short posts' categorization unprincipled.

success_hints: Ground every veridicality claim in an actual sampled (uri, text, label, prob, mass) row from data/gate.jsonl — never reason about hedges or quotation in the abstract.
When distinguishing use from mention, name a testable cue (quotation marks, attribution phrase, the has_context flag in context.py), not just assert the distinction exists.
Where the five candidates diverge on a real post, say which real posts each would flip relative to the gate's actual current verdict.
task_context: What does 'claim' mean in this pipeline? The gate (src/norvid_studier/gate_prompt.py) sorts 40,943 prefiltered Bluesky posts into claim/nonclaim and has now scored ~33k of them into data/gate.jsonl (each line: uri, label, prob, mass, top_token). Downstream, extract_prompt.py turns each claim into a 'commitment', pairing.py finds candidate contradictory pairs, and tension_prompt.py judges them. The acceptance criterion for the whole system is norvid_studies' words: 'found things I didn't notice but upon juxtaposition oh yeah those cant both be right'. Determine the top 5 candidate DEFINITIONS of 'claim' the gate could be operating on — not five example claims, five rival senses of the word — and rank them by how well each serves that acceptance criterion. Ground every candidate in the ACTUAL scored data: read data/gate.jsonl and data/posts.jsonl, sample real posts at various prob levels, and show which definition each real verdict is consistent with. Known symptoms to explain: questions still score YES despite an explicit NO rule; 'holy heck' scores as a claim; ~34% claim rate is ~10x the design estimate of belief-bearing posts (~3%); the rubric asks for 'asserts something that could be true or false, and that its author could be asked to defend' which conflates at least assertion-vs-question, proposition-vs-speech-act, and defensible-vs-sincere. Read docs/brainstorms/2026-07-29-norvid-studier-brainstorm.md for prior reasoning.
